title: Oscillating Grain Boundaries and Their Effects on Grain Growth: Observations in Skyrmion Bicrystals
content: Grain boundaries (GBs) play significant roles in various properties of polycrystalline materials [1,2]. At low homologous temperatures, GBs are usually considered to be essentially stationary, while at higher temperatures, they are presumed to move consistently by the curvature-driven mechanism, leading to grain growth according to the classic analysis by von Neumann and Mullins [3,4]. The von Neumann-Mullins theory assumes a uniform boundary model in which the GB energy per unit area is isotropic and constant over time [3,4]. Various mathematical models and computer simulations have addressed the variation of energy and mobility from boundary to boundary and changes in these properties with the orientation of the GB plane [5–7]. These all remain essentially uniform boundary models in which the properties of a particular GB remain constant as it migrates. However, recent discoveries have begun to challenge the von Neumann-Mullins theory [8–11], where the classic von Neumann-Mullins theory might be incomplete and fail to reflect the full range of intrinsic properties of GBs. Therefore, new models, atomic simulations, and experimental results are required to understand the fundamental behaviors of GBs.
